A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AssistanceZero and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Corresponding methods, equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original MBAG experiments, human-model evaluations, ablations, and a 16-participant human study (Sections 4–5; Appendices C–D).

after.justification: v2 retains those original simulation and human-study results, including the main comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: AssistanceZero retains the same four network heads, MCTS procedure, training losses, and reward-estimation approach (Section 4.2; Appendices A and E). No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CraftAssist-based MBAG house-building task, simulated human models, and human participants. No dataset, domain, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same PPO variants, PPO/AlphaZero/BC/piKL human models, pretrained and SFT assistants, and human-alone and expert-assistant conditions (Tables 1–3; Section 5).

E3.justification: The train/test-house separation, 1,000-episode main evaluations, metrics, training/search settings, and 16-participant within-subjects Latin-square study remain unchanged (Sections 4–5; Appendices C and E).

E4.justification: Both retain the same cross-human-model evaluations, BC component ablations, piKL sensitivity analysis, PPO ablations, and AssistanceZero recurrence and reward-prediction-penalty ablations (Appendix D). The illustrated behavioral examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same human-study 90% confidence intervals and one-sided t-test result, p < 0.05. Uncertainty reporting and seed or repeated-run disclosures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative findings are retained throughout. For example, Table 1 reports AssistanceZero at 79.8 ± 0.9 overall goal percentage and 158 ± 3 human actions in both versions. Appendix result pages are identical in text and rendering.

T1.justification: The assistance-game definitions, expected-return objective, loss equations, MCTS mathematics, and lower-variance reward-estimation argument remain unchanged (Section 2; Section 4.2; Appendix A).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable assistance-game solving, the MBAG benchmark, effective human modeling, and advantages over the evaluated PPO and imitation-learning approaches.

C2.justification: Interpretations of PPO's difficulties, BC compounding errors, and piKL's effectiveness are unchanged. Both retain the performance gap to expert human assistance, the explanation for omitting a full RLHF baseline, and the prospective LLM application discussion.

D1.justification: The code/model access link, environment implementation, data collection, network architecture, hyperparameters, and hardware-related evaluation details are unchanged. Appendices A–E contain no added or revised reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Changes such as Carroll 2020 to 2019 and Williams 2024 to 2025 accompany updated publication entries; they do not introduce different prior work.

P1.justification: v2 adds an ICML 2025 proceedings/copyright notice and updates bibliographic titles, author metadata, venues, and citation years. The scientific prose and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Main-text column and page breaks shift, and the bibliography is reformatted. Removing reference URLs eliminates the Ouyang et al. URL overlapping the adjacent column on v1 page 12. Figure designs, table structures, and appendix layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a limited editorial improvement through fuller publication references and removal of overlapping bibliography text visible on v1 page 12. Removing direct reference URLs reduces click-through convenience, but the readability improvement is concrete. The scientific evidence, conclusions, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
